newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Zwack says '97 profit on track, sales short.
newsitem.headline: Zwack says '97 profit on track, sales short.

text.p: Hungarian alcoholic-drinks producer Zwack Unicum Rt on Wednesday reported rising profits and sales for the first half of 1997 and a company official said it expected to meet the annual profit plan.
"We see our IAS annual pre-tax profit plan of 692 million forints ($3.5 million) as achievable," Ferenc Sarody, Zwack's controlling director, told Reuters.

However, the group does not expect to attain its annual sales target of 15.6 billion forints, he said. "It will fall somewhat short of the plan," Sarody said. "One reason behind this is a quite significant price competition in the area of commodities products."

Zwack's consolidated sales plan of 15.6 billion forints was made up of 15.2 billion forints of domestic sales while exports took up the rest. Six billion forints of total sales will go towards consumption tax, he said.

Sarody said he estimated sales would fall short of targets by around 300 million to 400 million forints but added profits will not reflect lower revenues because changes in the sales structure, with higher sales in more branded products at the expense of commodities products, will offset that.
Sarody said the lower revenues did not justify amending the sales target "because the sales plan is only one part (of the picture) and our owners are interested mainly in profits."

Zwack reported rising profits and sales, and said that demand from some parts of the legal spirits market had begun to increase. The group's consolidated IAS operating profits rose to 444 million forints in the first six months of 1997 from 378 million in the first six months of 1996, while its profit on ordinary activities before tax grew to 281 million from 202 million.

"The significant trend of a decreasing legal spirit market that started in 1995, is continuing in 1997," Zwack said in its earnings report. "However, some segments of the spirits market started to grow in the last six months."
Sarody said that the growth market was partly in imported products and partly in high-quality products.

"The reason behind is that the consumption tax on those items grew at a much smaller pace," he said. The change in the consumption tax structure affected the commodities product more than the branded and low spirit content products.

From this year the consumption tax depends only on the spirit content of the product as opposed to the previous practice of being based on the spirit content and a certain percentage of net sales prices .

Zwack said it continued to upgrade its product portfolio, adding that its new apricot brandy was launched in May as the first pure distillate from the renewed distillery in Kecskemet, central-east Hungary.
